 Judgment

The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.497/ 2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Alappuzha, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2. The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.11.2007.

According to the petitioner, on 11.11.2007, at about 4.20 p.m., while he was riding a motorcycle, an Maruti Omni Van bearing reg. number KL-04/P-8364 driven by Respondent No.2 in a rash and negligent manner, hit against the vehicle of the petitioner and as a result of which he fell down sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner , the 2 nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
was Rs.5,18,000/-.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs 1 to 3 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A24.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,97,055/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.

7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9.
Heard Sri.A.T. Anil Kumar, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/appellants, and Smt. Sarah Salvy, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy 2025:KER:24080 MACA NO.626 OF 2015 of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is regarding the income of the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to him,
the deceased was working as finishing worker of coir mats and mattings, earning Rs.9000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.5000/-.The learned counsel for the insurer
would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, during the year 2007 will come to Rs.6000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the petitioners could not prove the job or income of the deceased, as claimed in the OP, in the light of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.6000/-.
12.
In the accident the petitioner sustained fracture right femur and got segmental fracture right femur thigh.
Ext.A24 is the discharge summary.
As per discharge summary he was admitted at Lisie Hospital on 6.10.2009 and discharged 20.10.2009.
He was admitted with pain and suffering right 2025:KER:24080 MACA NO.626 OF 2015 thigh region H/O.MIPPO Surgery for segmental fracture femur with bone grafting 2 years back.

X-ray taken found non-union fracture at lower end of Rt.
Femur with implant failure and he had a two years old malunited hypertrophic non-union segmental fracture Rt.femur.

He was given treatment for removal of broken implant excision of non union (Hyper trophic callus) IF screw fixation & LC fixation (neutralization plate) under GA 9/10/09, the post operative period uneventful, knee mobilization started from 12.10.2009.
Ext.A25 is the OP ticket and Ext.A28 is the discharge summary issued Medical College Hospital, Alappuzha.
As per discharge summary he was first admitted there on 11.11.2007 and discharged on 1.12.2007.
Again he was admitted on 31.1.2008, treated with skeletal fraction followed by MIPPO and discharged on 13.2.2008.
He was admitted for un-united segmental fracture femur shaft (rt) and this discharge summary was issued by the Medical College Hospital, Kottayam.
13. He has also produced the disability certificate, it was marked as Ext.A23.

It is read as follows: 1.
Comminuted segmental fracture (Rt) femur.
He was treated with open reduction and internal fixation with plate and screw.

He underwent another surgery at Lisie Hospital, Ernakulam for non-union of 2025:KER:24080 MACA NO.626 OF 2015 the fracture with plate and screw and Lalu V.A vs Anilkumar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4731206/
3 grafting of bone after 2 years.

Now the patient complains of limbing and inability to flex the (Rt)
knee joint".
14. As per Exhibit A23 disability certificate the petitioner suffered 22% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board, and one of the doctors was examined as PW1.
The Tribunal, however, scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 15%, without assigning valid and cogent reasons.

The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.(See Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305).

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.
I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 22%.
15. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 37 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 15, 2025:KER:24080 MACA NO.626 OF 2015 as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.332640/-.
16. Towards loss of income, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.20000/- being the income for 4 months @Rs.5000/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 12 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.72000/-
(6000 x 12 months).
17. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25000/- and towards 'Bystander expense' and 'transportation' the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2000/- each.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.15000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
18. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 50 days in 3 sessions and in the meantime, he had undergone three operations.

Because of the injuries sustained, the 2025:KER:24080 MACA NO.626 OF 2015 percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life', 'bystander expense',
'transportation', and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.60000/-, Rs.40000/- Rs.7500/-, Rs.4000/-, and Rs.5000/- respectively.
19.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
20. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.6,17,195/- as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
